BEFORE constructing the Promise whose executor calls spawn(...) at line 608, with no await between them and readGitStatus itself synchronous (execSync) -- so within one command that before-sample unconditionally precedes its own child even existing, and JS single-threadedness means no other command can interleave between them. Confirmed the implementer's claim that 3 of 4 boundaries were already structurally ordered: before_writer<write and before_bystander<write follow from that synchronicity plus the pre-existing peer-start handshake (writer will not write until it observes bystander.start, which only a spawned bystander child can publish); write<after_writer follows trivially because the writer script performs the write itself before its own process.exit(0). The one boundary that needed a real fix, write<after_bystander, previously depended on a proxy marker plus Date.now()-based 30s deadline (bystander could give up and exit before the write actually landed). The fix (lines 177-207) has the bystander stat the writer's REAL file via fs.existsSync in a loop before publishing a per-self .observed marker, and the writer now waits on that marker (awaitObservedBy) before its own exit -- so both after-samples are gated on one confirmed on-disk observation, not a wall clock. Budget is now hrtime.bigint()-based (monotonic, immune to NTP/clock-jump) and set to 90s, strictly above the 60s per-command framework ceiling, so an unschedulable host hits the framework's own SIGTERM/SIGKILL+timedOut:true first rather than the script's internal exit(3).
